post.description: Forget the cached schema; the next completion or search rebuilds it.

get.description: Never called; exposes the WebSocket protocol models in OpenAPI.

The query contexts a tab can pick. `bucket` and `scope` name the tab's current one, listed first when the
schema snapshot does not have it.

post.description:
The collection the statement reads when it names exactly one (fully qualified, or resolved against the run's
context as SQL++ resolves it), else null. Pure: no connection, nothing logged.

schema.title: Response Statement Keyspace Couchbase Statement Keyspace Post

post.description: Sample a keyspace's documents (R-04-11): a manual action, whose result is kept for `GET /fields`.

get.description: The keyspace's last sample, or null when it has none (nothing samples by itself).

schema.title: Response Cached Fields Couchbase Fields Get

post.description: The document as stored: its exact text and META (spec §3.9.4). 404 `document_missing` when there is none.

Write the text over the document if it still has `cas`, or answer what the server would store instead
(`needs_confirmation`) until `confirmed`.

schema.title: Response Save Document Couchbase Documents Save Post

post.description: Create the document, previewed like a save; 409 `document_exists` when the ID is taken.

schema.title: Response Insert Document Couchbase Documents Insert Post

post.description: Delete the document if it still has `cas`.

The dump dialog's object list, what the header leaves out, the consistency and the warnings (the metadata
connection; nothing is written). 422 `not_supported` for an engine without dumps.
Show in Finder, for a file a completed dump of this backend run wrote (404 for any other path).
Run SQL file's dialog: the file's size, first lines and warnings. A read-only connection is refused (403).

get.description: Newest first: running and finished, until cleared (D-06-10).

schema.title: Response List Jobs Data Jobs Get

post.description: The WebSocket's `cancel`, for a job whose dialog is gone: a job that has ended is left as it is.
Forget the jobs that have ended (the Jobs list's Clear finished).
What the safety policy would say about each statement if the user had not confirmed it yet.
Whether a formatter's output may replace the original: only when its significant tokens are the same.

AppSettings.title: AppSettings
AppSettings.description:
The app preferences (`settings.json`). Persisted, so a newer build's extra fields are tolerated on read and
kept on write; input from the API stays strict.

ApplyEditsCommand.title: ApplyEditsCommand
ApplyEditsCommand.description:
Apply a previewed grid-edit plan (spec ⑤ §3.5): its statements exactly as previewed, in one transaction on this
session. A Cancel stops it until its COMMIT has been sent.

ConfirmationRequiredEvent.title: ConfirmationRequiredEvent
ConfirmationRequiredEvent.description: The statement was not run: resend it with `confirmed=true` once the user agreed. `finished(skipped)` follows.

ContextOption.title: ContextOption
ContextOption.description:
One entry of the query-context picker. `text` is `QueryContext(bucket, scope).text()`, so the frontend never
quotes a name (B13).

DangerReason.title: DangerReason
DangerReason.description: Why a statement is dangerous: the standard safety level asks before running it.

Dialect.title: Dialect
Dialect.description: The SQL dialect of an engine: how its statements are split, classified, completed and quoted.

DocumentChange.title: DocumentChange
DocumentChange.description: One thing the server would store differently from the edited text (spec §3.9.3, ruling C2).

DocumentSaved.title: DocumentSaved
DocumentSaved.description: A write that happened: the document's new CAS and its expiration.

DocumentView.title: DocumentView
DocumentView.description: One document as the server holds it (spec §3.9.2, R-04-2).

DumpCommand.title: DumpCommand
DumpCommand.description:
Dump a scope of this session's database to a SQL file (spec ⑥ §3.3): written through a temporary file, so a
dump that fails or is cancelled leaves no file and keeps any old one.

DumpHeader.title: DumpHeader
DumpHeader.description:
The first lines of a dump DbaGuy wrote (spec ⑥ §3.3.2), as Run SQL file's inspection reads them back: a hint
for the dialog, never a permission.

DumpObjectKinds.title: DumpObjectKinds
DumpObjectKinds.description:
Which objects besides tables a dump writes (R-06-2); a table's own sequences and column types always come
with it. Routines include MySQL events; views include SQL Server synonyms.

DumpPlan.title: DumpPlan
DumpPlan.description:
What a dump of a scope would write (POST /data/dump/plan): the dialog's object list and warnings. Read on the
metadata connection, outside any snapshot; the dump reads the catalog again inside its own.

`objects` are the objects the content writes under their own names, in the file's order: schemas, extensions,
collations, types, sequences, routines, tables, views, triggers, events, synonyms, rules, extended statistics and
policies. The parts of another object are left to it: a table's indexes, foreign keys, check constraints,
defaults and settings, a trigger's state, a sequence's owner and value, an identity's value, a table's row-level
security switch, SQLite's header settings (user_version, application_id). A data-only plan lists the tables alone,
parents first. `not_included` is the header's Not included list, word for word.

DumpPlanObject.title: DumpPlanObject
DumpPlanObject.description: One object a dump writes under its own name, as the dump dialog lists it.

DumpScope.title: DumpScope
DumpScope.description:
What a dump covers (spec ⑥ §3.3.1): a whole database (PostgreSQL, SQL Server), one schema (MySQL: a database;
SQLite: main), or named tables and views of one schema.

EditOutcomeEvent.title: EditOutcomeEvent
EditOutcomeEvent.description: How an apply ended (spec ⑤ R-05-6): sent once, right before the request's `session_state` and `finished`.

ExecutionSchema.title: ExecutionSchema
ExecutionSchema.description: Exposes the WebSocket protocol in OpenAPI so the frontend types are generated.

ExportCommand.title: ExportCommand
ExportCommand.description: Run `sql` again on this session and write its whole result, as raw values, to the file at `path`.

FieldPath.title: FieldPath
FieldPath.description: One field path of a sample: how many documents have it and with which JSON kinds.

FieldSample.title: FieldSample
FieldSample.description: A manual sample of a keyspace (R-04-11): the field paths derived in Python from the documents read.

FileInspection.title: FileInspection
FileInspection.description: What Run SQL file's dialog shows of a file before it runs (POST /data/run-file/inspect).

GuardReason.title: GuardReason
GuardReason.description:
Why the safety policy asks for confirmation (a danger, or any non-read statement at the strict level) or blocks
a statement (a read-only connection). Every `DangerReason` is one, with the same value.

JobError.title: JobError
JobError.description: One statement that failed: where, the server's code and its own text (shown, never logged above DEBUG).

JobInfo.title: JobInfo
JobInfo.description: A job of this backend run, as the Jobs list shows it (GET /data/jobs).

JobObject.title: JobObject
JobObject.description: One object of a dump, with the rows written for it.

JobOutcomeEvent.title: JobOutcomeEvent
JobOutcomeEvent.description: How a job ended (R-06-12): sent once, right before the request's `session_state` and `finished`.

JobProgressEvent.title: JobProgressEvent
JobProgressEvent.description: How far a job is (D-06-11): at most every 250 ms, and as each object starts and ends. Cumulative counts.

Keyspace.title: Keyspace
Keyspace.description: A collection by its three names. Frozen: it is the key of the field-sample cache.

ProfileSecretsInput.title: ProfileSecretsInput
ProfileSecretsInput.description: `None` keeps the stored secret; an empty string clears it.

ProgressEvent.title: ProgressEvent
ProgressEvent.description: An export has written `rows` rows so far; sent after every 10,000 rows.

QueryContext.title: QueryContext
QueryContext.description:
Couchbase: the bucket (and scope) that unqualified keyspace names resolve against, sent with every request
(D-04-5: a structure, because a bucket name may hold a dot).

RunFileCommand.title: RunFileCommand
RunFileCommand.description:
Run a SQL file on this session, a statement at a time (spec ⑥ §3.4): all of it in one transaction, or each
statement on its own (stopping at an error, or skipping it). Statements before `from_statement` are read, never
sent.

SampleLimits.title: SampleLimits
SampleLimits.description: What bounds a sample, as the backend has it: the UI words what a sample left out with these numbers.

SavePreview.title: SavePreview
SavePreview.description: What the server would store instead of the edited text: nothing is written until the user confirms.

SessionStateEvent.title: SessionStateEvent
SessionStateEvent.description:
The session's transaction state: sent right before every `finished` and every pause, on attach and after an
idle rollback.

StagedCell.title: StagedCell
StagedCell.description: A staged cell as `workspace.json` keeps it: one value of at most MAX_VALUE_CHARS (D-05-11), not a request's 4x.

StagedEditsFile.title: StagedEditsFile
StagedEditsFile.description:
A table-data tab's staged grid edits in `workspace.json` (spec ⑤ §3.7, ruling H6): the changes as staged (an
UPDATE under its row's DELETE included), the key they were staged on, and whether the last commit's outcome is
unknown. Bounded like a commit (D-05-11) and by MAX_STAGED_CHARS in all: the frontend writes none that is larger
(`savedEdits`), and the workspace repair drops one this model refuses rather than the tab (B40).

StatementParams.title: StatementParams
StatementParams.description:
Typed parameters of one statement (R-10): JSON literal texts, sent unchanged. Content is checked by the worker
(`invalid_params`), only the shape here.

StoppedAt.title: StoppedAt
StoppedAt.description: Where a run stopped: the statement that failed, was cancelled or was not sent.

WorkspaceState.title: WorkspaceState
WorkspaceState.description: The open tabs (`workspace.json`), written whole every few seconds so that a crash loses nothing.
